label: The lightness ladder pre-exists on both paths, calibrated to the same numbers: exempt-typo, Level 0 (score <= 24), Level 1 (<= 44), Level 2 (<= 69), Level 3 (70+), with one scorer owning the boundaries.

No mechanism needs to invent lightness; it needs to read the level one scorer already prints. The scorer is already referenced from four chat-path entry points, so a mechanism that consumes its answer inherits the ladder and a mechanism that does not must restate it.
Both paths already say skip this at Level 1 in the same words, so Level 1 is not where the chat path loses protection; the gap iteration 1 found sits above Level 1's business.

Level 1 costs four documents and ~49.6 KB of template (17,503 + 15,050 + 11,872 + 5,195), and the apparent three-vs-four required-file conflict resolves by the 'created after implementation' qualifier both sources carry.
The opt-out precedent is a scope-bound phrase list on one existing AGENTS.md line, and it covers memory loading only, so it cannot already serve a documentation-gate opt-out.

The only fully data-driven opt-out in the repo is the advisor prompt policy: EXACT_SKIP_COMMANDS plus casual-acknowledgement, work-intent and governance-marker sets, 91 lines / 1,486 bytes read by the CLI not the model, with env-overridable path and thresholds and a master kill switch above it.

A hook gets automatic lightness for free because it declines short prompts, casual acknowledgements and skip commands before spawning the CLI; a text gate cannot, because its text is read every turn whether it fires or not.

Gate 3 Option D is a session-scoped opt-out in practice because the answer holds for the entire session and is re-asked only on new task, different feature, a different folder or an explicit ask; the missing piece is a reusable phrase, not a new permission model.

Validator-carried enforcement is the only mechanism with a provably zero marginal cost at Level 1: the validator already runs at completion with level-scoped rules and per-level file lists, so a new rule adds neither prompt tokens nor an extra command run.

Invoking the command on a typo fix is the heaviest option: 830 lines / 60,098 bytes for implement and 1,444 / 93,496 for complete, 12 confirm-mode checkpoints and a rule forbidding skipped steps, with auto/autopilot skipping confirm blocks but not steps - so its lightness lever is a mode argument rather than new text.

Under the validator mechanism the opt-out and the lightness control collapse into one lever, a declared level, so no new vocabulary is needed; under a text gate or shared reference the opt-out must be a phrase added to the existing scoped bypass-phrase line.

The proposed Q4 plan-shape fix carries no level qualifier and would charge Level 1 as well: the plan-shape section states its three-phase requirement and heading-grep verify unconditionally, so it needs a level qualifier on its acceptance line before it lands.
A protection mechanism added to the chat path must read the level rather than restate the ladder, or Level 1 pays the Level 3 price.
The only opt-out shapes that exist in this repo are a scope-bound bypass phrase on AGENTS.md line 108 and a declared level consumed by the validator; any third shape is new vocabulary.

note: Level 1 required-file lists read as three in implement.yaml and four in folder-structure.md; the difference is implementation-summary.md, which both mark as created after implementation and complete.yaml requires at completion. Resolved by qualifier, no LOGIC-SYNC decision required.
